questions.text: Which is the largest planet in our solar system?
questions.fact: Jupiter is more than twice as massive as all the other planets combined.

questions.text: How many hearts does an octopus have?
questions.fact: Two hearts pump blood through the gills and the third pumps it around the body.

questions.text: At sea level, water boils at what temperature in degrees Celsius?
questions.source: NIST — Temperature scales (water boils at 100 °C / 212 °F at standard pressure)
questions.fact: 212 is the boiling point in Fahrenheit — a classic trap!

questions.text: What is the closest star to Earth?
questions.fact: Proxima Centauri is the closest star beyond the Sun, about 4.2 light-years away.

questions.text: What is the hardest naturally occurring mineral?
questions.fact: Diamond is a 10 on the Mohs scale, the top of the scale.

questions.text: Which gas do plants take in from the air to make their food?
questions.fact: Plants use sunlight to turn carbon dioxide and water into sugar, releasing oxygen.

questions.text: How many bones are in a typical adult human body?
questions.fact: Babies are born with around 300 bones; many fuse together as they grow.

questions.text: What is the fastest land animal?
questions.fact: Cheetahs can sprint at around 100–110 km/h (60–70 mph) in short bursts.

questions.text: Which planet is known as the Red Planet?
questions.fact: Iron oxide (rust) in its dust and rocks gives Mars its reddish colour.

questions.text: How many legs does a spider have?
questions.fact: Insects have six legs; spiders are arachnids, not insects.

questions.text: What is the largest animal living on Earth today?
questions.fact: Blue whales can grow to around 30 metres (nearly 100 feet) long.

questions.text: What is the chemical symbol for gold?
questions.source: Royal Society of Chemistry — Periodic Table: Gold
questions.fact: Au comes from 'aurum', the Latin word for gold. Ag is silver.

questions.text: Which planet is the hottest in our solar system?
questions.fact: Mercury is closer to the Sun, but Venus's thick carbon-dioxide atmosphere traps heat, making it hotter.

questions.text: Botanically speaking, what is a tomato?
questions.fact: Botanically, a tomato is a berry — the fruit of the tomato plant.

questions.text: Which of these places has NO wild penguins?
questions.fact: Galápagos penguins live right on the equator, but no penguins live wild in the Arctic.

questions.text: Sound cannot travel through which of these?
questions.source: NASA — Sound needs a medium to travel through
questions.fact: Sound is a vibration of matter, so with no matter, there's no sound.

questions.text: Roughly how long ago did the non-bird dinosaurs die out?
questions.source: Natural History Museum, London — How an asteroid ended the age of the dinosaurs
questions.fact: Birds are living dinosaurs — they're descended from the survivors.

questions.text: How many players does each team have on the field in a soccer (association football) match?
questions.source: IFAB Laws of the Game — Law 3: The Players

questions.text: How high above the floor is a regulation basketball rim?
questions.source: NBA Official Rules / FIBA Official Basketball Rules
questions.fact: Every level, from the NBA to the Olympics, uses the same 10-foot rim.

questions.text: How many rings are on the Olympic flag?
questions.source: International Olympic Committee — Olympic Charter (the Olympic symbol)
questions.fact: The five interlaced rings represent the union of the five continents.

questions.text: How long is an official marathon?
In golf, what is a score of one stroke under par on a hole called?
questions.fact: An eagle is two under par, and a bogey is one over.

questions.text: In tennis, what word means a score of zero?
questions.source: International Tennis Federation — Rules of Tennis (scoring)

questions.text: How long is a standard professional soccer match, not counting stoppage time?
questions.source: IFAB Laws of the Game — Law 7: The Duration of the Match
questions.fact: Two halves of 45 minutes each.

questions.text: In baseball, how many strikes make a strikeout?
What is the highest possible score in a single game of ten-pin bowling?
questions.source: United States Bowling Congress — Playing rules
questions.fact: A perfect game takes 12 strikes in a row.

questions.text: Which sport uses a shuttlecock?
questions.source: Badminton World Federation — Laws of Badminton

questions.text: In American football, how many points is a touchdown worth?
questions.fact: The 7th point usually comes from the extra-point kick after the touchdown.

questions.text: In which city were the first modern Olympic Games held, in 1896?
The Tour de France is a famous race in which sport?
questions.fact: The race was first held in 1903.

questions.text: How many players per team are on the court in indoor volleyball?
questions.fact: Beach volleyball is played two-a-side.

questions.text: Sumo wrestling is traditionally associated with which country?
questions.fact: Many modern sumo champions have come from Mongolia, but sumo is a Japanese tradition.

questions.text: How many holes are played in a standard round of golf?
questions.source: The R&A / USGA — Rules of Golf

questions.text: In ice hockey, what do players shoot into the goal?
questions.source: International Ice Hockey Federation — Official Rule Book
questions.fact: Curling is the sport that uses stones on ice.

questions.text: In "Toy Story", what is the name of the cowboy doll?
What is the name of the talking snowman in Disney's "Frozen"?
questions.fact: Sven is Kristoff's reindeer.

questions.text: In "The Lion King", what kind of animal is Timon?
questions.source: Walt Disney Animation Studios — The Lion King (1994)
questions.fact: His best friend Pumbaa is the warthog.

questions.text: How many members were in The Beatles' famous lineup?
questions.fact: John, Paul, George and Ringo.

questions.text: Which Hogwarts house is Harry Potter sorted into?
questions.source: J.K. Rowling — Harry Potter and the Philosopher's Stone (1997)

questions.text: In "SpongeBob SquarePants", what does SpongeBob live in?
questions.fact: His best friend Patrick lives under a rock.

questions.text: In "Shrek", Shrek's chatty sidekick is a talking what?
What is the name of Mario's brother in Nintendo's games?
What was Pixar's first feature-length film?

questions.text: In the 1939 film "The Wizard of Oz", what colour are Dorothy's magic slippers?
questions.source: Smithsonian National Museum of American History — Ruby Slippers
questions.fact: In L. Frank Baum's original book they were silver — the film changed them to show off Technicolor.

questions.text: Pikachu is which type of Pokémon?
Which small green Jedi Master trains Luke Skywalker in "The Empire Strikes Back"?
In "Finding Nemo", what kind of fish is Nemo?
questions.fact: Dory is the blue tang.

questions.text: How many keys does a standard modern piano have?
questions.fact: 52 white keys and 36 black keys.

questions.source: Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences — The Oscar statuette

questions.text: Paddington Bear originally comes from which country?
questions.source: Michael Bond — A Bear Called Paddington (1958)
questions.fact: He arrives in London from "darkest Peru" with a label saying "Please look after this bear".

questions.text: What is the largest ocean on Earth?
questions.source: NOAA — How big is the Pacific Ocean?
questions.fact: The Pacific is larger than all of Earth's land area combined.

questions.text: What is the capital city of Australia?
questions.fact: Canberra was purpose-built as a compromise between rivals Sydney and Melbourne.

questions.text: Counting cold deserts too, what is the largest desert on Earth?

questions.fact: A desert is defined by how little precipitation it gets, not by heat. The Sahara is the largest hot desert.

questions.text: Using the model most English-speaking schools teach, how many continents are there?
What is the highest mountain above sea level?
questions.fact: Everest's summit is about 8,849 metres (29,032 feet) above sea level.

questions.text: What is the capital city of Canada?
What is the smallest country in the world by area?
questions.source: CIA World Factbook — Holy See (Vatican City)
questions.fact: It covers less than half a square kilometre.

questions.text: Which country has the largest population?
questions.source: United Nations DESA — World Population Prospects

questions.text: In which U.S. city is the Statue of Liberty?
questions.source: U.S. National Park Service — Statue of Liberty National Monument

questions.text: Which country is famously shaped like a boot?
The Sahara Desert is on which continent?
How many states are in the United States?
The Great Barrier Reef lies off the coast of which country?
questions.source: Great Barrier Reef Marine Park Authority
questions.fact: It's the world's largest coral reef system.

questions.text: What is the capital city of Japan?
questions.fact: Kyoto was the imperial capital for over a thousand years before Tokyo.

questions.text: In which country is Machu Picchu?
questions.source: UNESCO World Heritage Centre — Historic Sanctuary of Machu Picchu

questions.text: Mount Kilimanjaro, Africa's highest mountain, is in which country?
questions.source: UNESCO World Heritage Centre — Kilimanjaro National Park
questions.fact: It's often photographed from Kenya, but the mountain itself is in Tanzania.

questions.text: Which imaginary line divides Earth into the Northern and Southern Hemispheres?
questions.fact: The Prime Meridian divides the Eastern and Western Hemispheres.

questions.text: In which year did astronauts first land on the Moon?
Who was the first person to walk on the Moon?
questions.fact: Buzz Aldrin followed him about 20 minutes later.

questions.text: Who was the first President of the United States?
In which year did the Titanic sink?
questions.fact: It sank on its maiden voyage after hitting an iceberg.

questions.text: Who made the first controlled, powered airplane flights in 1903?
questions.source: Smithsonian National Air and Space Museum — The 1903 Wright Flyer

questions.text: Who was the first woman to win a Nobel Prize?
questions.source: The Nobel Prize — Marie Curie facts
questions.fact: She won in Physics in 1903 and again in Chemistry in 1911.

In which year did the Berlin Wall fall?

questions.text: What was the main language of ancient Rome?
Who was granted the first U.S. patent for the telephone in 1876?
questions.source: Library of Congress — Alexander Graham Bell Family Papers

questions.text: Magna Carta was sealed in 1215 by which English king?
Who was the first human to travel into space?
questions.source: European Space Agency — Yuri Gagarin, first human in space (1961)

questions.source: U.S. National Park Service — Statue of Liberty history

questions.text: Who led the 1922 discovery of King Tutankhamun's tomb?
questions.source: Griffith Institute, University of Oxford — Tutankhamun: Anatomy of an Excavation

questions.text: Which of the Seven Wonders of the Ancient World is still standing?
questions.source: Encyclopaedia Britannica — Seven Wonders of the World

questions.text: Around 1440, Johannes Gutenberg developed which invention in Europe?
options: The printing press with movable type

questions.text: Why are flamingos pink?
options: Pigments in the food they eat
questions.source: San Diego Zoo Wildlife Alliance — Flamingo
questions.fact: Flamingo chicks hatch grey or white and turn pink from carotenoids in algae and shrimp.

questions.text: Which food can stay edible for thousands of years if it's sealed?
questions.source: Smithsonian Magazine — The Science Behind Honey's Eternal Shelf Life
questions.fact: Archaeologists have found still-edible honey in ancient Egyptian tombs.

questions.text: Botanically, which of these is a true berry?
questions.fact: Strawberries and raspberries aren't true berries — but bananas are!

questions.text: Which animal produces cube-shaped poop?
questions.source: Yang et al., "Intestines of non-uniform stiffness mold the corners of wombat feces", Soft Matter (2021)

questions.text: What colour is an octopus's blood?

questions.text: Why is the Eiffel Tower slightly taller in summer?
options: It sinks into the ground in winter
Painters add extra layers each summer
questions.source: Official Eiffel Tower website (toureiffel.paris) — The tower's movements

questions.text: Which animal has fingerprints so similar to ours that they could confuse investigators?
questions.source: Henneberg, Lambert & Leigh, "Fingerprint homoplasy: koalas and humans", Nature (1996)

questions.text: Venus takes about 243 Earth days to spin once on its axis. How does that compare with its year (one trip around the Sun)?
options: It's a tenth of its year
questions.fact: A Venus year is only about 225 Earth days.

questions.text: Bananas are very slightly radioactive. Which element in them causes this?
questions.source: U.S. Environmental Protection Agency — Radioactivity in food

questions.text: Butterflies taste their food using their…
questions.fact: Taste sensors on their feet tell a butterfly if a leaf is good for laying eggs on.

questions.text: In the 1830s, tomato ketchup was sold in the United States as what?
questions.source: Smithsonian Magazine — Ketchup was once sold as medicine (Andrew F. Smith, The Tomato in America)

questions.text: Roughly how much does the water in one fluffy cumulus cloud weigh?
options: About as much as a car

questions.source: Li et al., PLoS Genetics (2005) — Monell Chemical Senses Center

questions.source: Encyclopaedia Britannica — Rainbow (Isaac Newton's seven colours)
